messages:
Maya: quick heads-up — bringing up 'auric' embedding (int6 compact) on staging. Seeing a small but consistent recall@10 drop on short queries vs our baseline. anyone available to help triage?

Liam: can you paste the delta numbers + which eval set? :eyes:

Maya: shortquery-holdout-10k. baseline (float32) -> auric-int6 (per-tensor): recall@1 0.42 -> 0.395, recall@10 0.78 -> 0.74, silhouette 0.21 -> 0.18. cluster compactness metric decreased ~3.5%.

Sophia: which quant backend? per-channel or per-tensor? int6 often sensitive to scale/zero-point choices. :thinking:

Maya: exported via ONNX int6 per-tensor (default export script), runtime on dedicated-staging-a100. no additional post-quant calibration beyond clamp. command I used: 

```bash
./eval_embs.py \n  --model auric-int6.onnx \n  --dataset shortquery-holdout-10k \n  --knn 10 \n  --metrics recall@1,recall@10,silhouette,compactness
```

Liam: ok. can you share the embedding norm distribution (hist) and a small sample of neighbours for failed cases?

Maya: uploaded a quick snapshot: https://redwood-internal/snapshots/auric/int6/shortquery/hist.png — short sample: query 'how to reset pwd' neighbors are noisy (one case: neighbor from different intent).

Sophia: two hypotheses: (1) quantization scaled some projection head weights unevenly -> centroid shift; (2) L2 norm drift due to folded batchnorms. try L2-normalize after dequant and also try per-channel quantization. small code tweak: 

```python
embs = np.load('embs.npy')
# normalize before KNN
embs = embs / np.linalg.norm(embs, axis=1, keepdims=True)
```

Raj: fwiw we saw a similar pattern on marlin-int6 rollout — switching to per-channel reduced recall gap by ~2.5pts. also try whitening/centering using holdout mean before indexing.

Sophia: also check tokenization edgecases — short queries sometimes lose a leading token if whitespace/newline behavior changed between exports. that can flip a nearest neighbour.

EvalBot: automated comparison job completed for auric-int6-perchannel run triggered by @Maya. results: recall@1 0.412, recall@10 0.772, silhouette 0.20, compactness delta -1.8%. drift flagged for shorttail cohort. log: https://ci.redwood/evals/5798642100/log

Maya: nice — per-channel almost closes the gap on recall@10. i'll run additional runs with: (a) post-quant L2 normalization, (b) whitening using train-set mean, (c) per-channel asymmetric scaling.

Liam: can you also run a small k-fold on the holdout to ensure this isn't random sample variance? 3 seeds should be enough.

Maya: yep scheduling 3-seed k-fold now, will include topk distribution plots and a shortlist of queries that flip neighbors. timeline ~2 hours.

Sophia: if per-channel + L2 norm still underperforms, consider retraining with slight embedding temperature adjustment or adding a small quant-aware finetune pass.

Raj: agree. also check index build params (hnsw ef/search_k) — lower recall can be compounded by index config differences between runs.

Maya: good call — index params matched but I'll re-run build to be sure. will report back with short report and suggested flag to ship (per-channel) or hold. :thumbsup:
